title: How to Export & Analyze Claude Enterprise Usage Data (CSV + Analytics API)
summary: How to export Claude Enterprise usage data: the spend report CSV, the Claude Analytics API, Claude Code analytics and the Compliance API, step by step.
body_markdown:
The Claude Analytics API is how Claude Enterprise organizations pull usage data into their own warehouse or BI tool: per-user daily activity across chat, projects, Claude Code and Cowork, plus active-user summaries and cost reports. For a one-off export, Owners and Primary Owners can download a per-user CSV spend report from Settings > Analytics. Audit data, including chat content, sits in a separate Compliance API.


This guide walks through each export path step by step, explains which API key you need (they are not interchangeable), covers Claude Code analytics for Claude Console organizations, and shows how to turn the export into adoption and proficiency measurement.


**Key takeaways**


- **CSV spend report:** Settings > Analytics > Export spend report. One row per person per model, with requests, tokens and spend, up to 90 days back, one-day delay.
- **Claude Enterprise Analytics API:** per-user daily activity, active-user summaries, project, skill and connector usage, and cost reports. Only the Primary Owner can create the key, which carries the read:analytics scope.
- **Claude Code Analytics API and Usage and Cost API:** for Claude Console organizations, using an Admin API key.
- **Compliance API:** audit events, chats and files for security and legal teams, with its own Compliance Access Key.
- None of these compares Claude with Copilot, Gemini or ChatGPT or links usage to your org chart. That is the layer[Worklytics](https://www.worklytics.co/measureai) adds, using metadata only.


## Where Claude usage data lives, and which key you need


Anthropic splits reporting across several surfaces, and each uses a different key created by a different role ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api) ):


- **Analytics dashboard (claude.ai):** charts for adoption, product use and spend, with a CSV spend report export. No key needed.
- **Claude Enterprise Analytics API:** engagement, adoption, cost and usage data for Claude Enterprise organizations. Uses an Analytics API key created by the Primary Owner in claude.ai > Organization settings > API.
- **Claude Code Analytics API and Usage and Cost API:** part of the Admin API for Claude Console (Claude Platform) organizations. Uses an Admin API key created by an organization admin in the Claude Console.
- **Compliance API:** audit activity, chats, files and projects for security, eDiscovery and legal teams. Uses a Compliance Access Key with scoped permissions ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api-access) ).


The key types are not interchangeable. An Admin API key cannot call the Claude Enterprise Analytics API, and an Analytics API key cannot call the Admin API. If every analytics call returns an authentication error, check the key type before you debug your code.


## How to export Claude Enterprise usage data as a CSV


The CSV is the fastest way to get per-user data and needs no engineering time. Usage analytics are available to Enterprise Owners, Primary Owners and Admins, although Admins cannot see spend ([Anthropic](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12883420-view-usage-analytics-for-team-and-enterprise-plans) ). To export the spend report:


1. Go to **Settings > Analytics** (click your initials in the lower left corner, then Analytics).
2. Scroll down to the **How much is Claude costing?** section.
3. Click **Export spend report** .
4. Select a time period: MTD, Last Month, Last 90 Days or Custom. Custom ranges go back up to 90 days, and the most recent data is from yesterday.
5. Click **Download** .


Each row is one person's usage of one model, summed across the date range. The fields are the user's email and account UUID, product (such as Chat, Claude Code, Cowork or Office Agents, which combines the Claude add-ins for Excel, PowerPoint and Word), model and model family, request count, prompt tokens, completion tokens, net spend and gross spend in USD.


Two plan details prevent misreadings. On usage-based Enterprise plans, the export covers your organization's full usage. On seat-based Enterprise plans, the spend report only appears when usage credits are enabled, and it reflects only spend beyond the seat allotment. If your totals look implausibly low, that scope difference is usually the reason.


The dashboard has two more exports worth knowing: the Claude Code leaderboard (pull requests and lines of code) can export users, and each in-product survey under Analytics > Surveys has its own CSV export.


## How to pull the data with the Claude Enterprise Analytics API


When the analysis needs to live in a warehouse, refresh on a schedule or join with HR data, use the[Claude Enterprise Analytics API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api) . It is available to Claude Enterprise organizations. Engagement and adoption data covers all Enterprise plans, while the cost and usage endpoints apply to usage-based plans (on seat-based plans they reflect usage credits only).


1. Sign in to claude.ai as the **Primary Owner** . Only the Primary Owner can enable API access and create Analytics API keys.
2. Go to **Organization settings > API** , enable public API access and create an Analytics API key. Keys carry the **read:analytics** scope. Copy the secret and store it in your secrets manager.
3. Call endpoints under api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/analytics/, passing the key in the **x-api-key** header and the **anthropic-version** header on every request. For example, the List User Activity endpoint returns per-user activity for one day:


curl "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/analytics/users?date=2026-10-15" --header "x-api-key: $ANALYTICS_API_KEY" --header "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01"


To get one row per user for a whole period instead of one day, pass starting_date and ending_date (up to 366 days apart) in place of date ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/analytics/users/list) ).


What you get ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api) ):


- **User activity:** per-user daily metrics for chat (conversations, messages, projects, files, artifacts), Claude Code (sessions, commits, pull requests, lines of code, tool actions), Cowork and other Claude products.
- **Activity summaries:** daily, weekly and monthly active users, seat counts and pending invites.
- **Project, skill and connector usage.**
- **Cost and usage reports:** per-user and organization-level tokens and cost over time.


Plan your pulls around freshness. Data starts on January 1, 2026. Engagement and adoption data for a day is typically ready around 13:00 to 13:30 UTC the next day. Cost and usage data usually lands within four hours but can take up to 24, and values can change until about 7 days after the end of the month, so use closed months for invoice-grade totals. The rate limit is 60 requests per minute per organization. Field-level schemas are in the[Analytics API reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/analytics) .


One gap is explicit: if your organization runs Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock, that activity does not appear in the Claude Enterprise Analytics API.


## Claude Console organizations: Claude Code Analytics API and Usage and Cost API


If your teams use Claude through the Claude Console (Claude Platform) rather than claude.ai, use the Admin API instead. An organization admin creates an Admin API key on the Admin keys page in the Console.


- **Claude Code Analytics API** (/v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code): one record per user per day with sessions, lines of code added and removed, commits, pull requests, accepted and rejected tool actions, and tokens and estimated cost by model. Data typically appears within an hour ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/claude-code-analytics-api) ).
- **Usage and Cost API** (/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages and /v1/organizations/cost_report): token usage by model, workspace and API key, and costs in USD, typically within about 5 minutes ([Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/usage-cost-api) ).


Claude Code used with a Claude subscription plan (Team or Enterprise) is attributed to the claude.ai organization, so the Admin API does not return it. For Enterprise, use the Claude Enterprise Analytics API above. For a deeper guide to developer metrics, see[how to track Claude Code usage](https://www.worklytics.co/blog/tracking-claude-code-usage) .


## **A Framework for Analyzing the Export: Adoption, Proficiency, Leverage**


Raw rows do not answer executive questions; a measurement framework does. Worklytics structures[AI adoption measurement](https://www.worklytics.co/measureai) in three stages, and the Claude export maps cleanly onto the first two.


*The Worklytics three-stage model for measuring AI impact: adoption, proficiency, and leverage.*


**Adoption** asks what share of the team uses AI daily, weekly, or monthly. From the CSV or the activity summaries endpoint, count distinct users with at least one request in the window and divide by assigned seats. This immediately produces the list every admin needs before renewal: seats with zero requests in 90 days. **Proficiency** asks how deeply active users work with the tool. Requests per active day, token consumption per user, and product mix carry the signal here, because a user logging 40 short Chat requests represents a different maturity level than one whose Claude Code sessions produce commits and pull requests. **Leverage** asks whether the organization is getting more done with AI than without it, and this is where the export stops. Anthropic reports what happened inside Claude and nothing about output. Answering the leverage question requires joining usage records to calendar, collaboration, and delivery signals, which is the analysis layer Worklytics automates through its[productivity measurement](https://www.worklytics.co/productivity) capabilities.


## What to compare your Claude export against


An adoption rate means little on its own. Three comparisons make it useful:


- **Other AI tools in the same teams.** Many employees use more than one AI assistant. A team that looks quiet in Claude may be doing the same work in ChatGPT, Copilot or Gemini, so read a single-vendor export as part of the picture, not all of it.
- **Your own trend.** Weekly active users and active days per week matter more as a direction over 8 to 12 weeks than as a single number.
- **Peer organizations.** Worklytics peer benchmarking, which places your AI adoption against similar organizations, is available in beta through[Worklytics Benchmark](https://www.worklytics.co/benchmarks) .

## Where CSV exports and the Analytics API stop


The native exports are accurate for what they cover, and their limits are structural rather than fixable with better queries.


*Example: multi-tool AI use in a Worklytics sample report. Demo data.*


1. **Vendor-isolated.** The data describes Claude and nothing else, while most organizations also pay for Copilot, Gemini or ChatGPT.
2. **Short history in the dashboard.** The spend report reaches back 90 days, and API data starts on January 1, 2026. Long-term trends need you to store pulls yourself.
3. **No task classification.** The data counts requests, tokens, sessions, skills and connectors, but it does not say whether Claude drafted emails, analyzed data or wrote code outside Claude Code's own metrics.
4. **No organizational hierarchy.** Users appear by email, so every department or manager cut depends on a join against your HRIS that you build and maintain.
5. **No outcome linkage.** Nothing in the export connects usage to delivery speed, meeting load or collaboration patterns, which is what executives mean when they ask whether Claude is working.


## **Turning Claude Exports Into Organization-Wide AI Measurement With Worklytics**


Worklytics connects to Claude through the Compliance API and the Claude Enterprise Analytics API, and to Claude Code through Anthropic's Admin API usage reporting. It brings that usage together with Copilot, Gemini, ChatGPT Enterprise and coding assistants, resolves every user against your organizational hierarchy, and handles the joins the raw export leaves to you. Three capabilities map onto the gaps above.


**Adoption tracking by team and role.** The[AI adoption dashboard](https://www.worklytics.co/measureai) aggregates active use across every connected AI tool and surfaces adoption gaps at the department level rather than as a flat list of email addresses, so enablement budgets target the specific functions where uptake has stalled instead of spreading evenly across the company.


*Worklytics sample report: Sales, HR, and Marketing show the lowest AI penetration, surfacing adoption gaps by department across connected tools.*


**Work classification.** Worklytics automatically classifies AI activity into work categories such as coding, research, analysis, summarization, drafting, and email creation. This converts the export’s token counts into the language leadership actually uses: which workflows AI is accelerating, and where usage remains shallow.


*Worklytics insight view: AI usage classified into work categories, showing what each tool is actually used for.*


**Impact measurement.** Pairing classified usage with delivery, collaboration, and calendar signals shows which tools are moving real work forward, which is the evidence a renewal conversation about Claude seats actually needs. Worklytics pairs this with the[AI ROI calculator](https://www.worklytics.co/ai-roi-calculator) for teams that want to model expected returns before expanding licenses.


*Worklytics impact view: monthly cost versus estimated value generated per tool, including Claude.*


All of this runs on usage metadata only. Worklytics never stores prompt or completion content, pseudonymizes personal identifiers (hashed with SHA-256) before analysis, and shows results only for groups above a minimum size (typically 5 to 8 people). That keeps the program positioned as measurement rather than surveillance. Engineering leaders who need depth on the coding side can follow the guide to[tracking Claude Code usage](https://www.worklytics.co/blog/tracking-claude-code-usage) , and admins comparing the dashboard and Compliance API in more detail should read the full guide to[tracking Claude Enterprise usage](https://www.worklytics.co/blog/track-if-employees-are-using-claude-enterprise) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the Claude Analytics API?


The Claude Enterprise Analytics API gives Claude Enterprise organizations programmatic access to per-user daily activity, active-user summaries, project, skill and connector usage, and cost reports. Endpoints live under api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/analytics/ and use an Analytics API key with the read:analytics scope. Claude Console organizations use the separate Claude Code Analytics API and Usage and Cost API with an Admin API key.


### Who can export Claude Enterprise usage data?


Owners and Primary Owners can export the CSV spend report from Settings > Analytics, and Enterprise Admins can view analytics except spend. Only the Primary Owner can enable API access and create an Analytics API key.


### How far back does Claude usage data go?


The dashboard spend report reaches back up to 90 days, with the latest data from yesterday. The Claude Enterprise Analytics API has data from January 1, 2026 onward. For longer trends, store the data in your own warehouse or use a platform that keeps the history for you.


### Does the Claude export include conversation content?


No. The CSV and the Analytics API return usage metadata such as users, products, models, requests, tokens and cost. Chats, files and audit events are only available through the Compliance API, using a Compliance Access Key created by the Primary Owner or an organization owner.


### Can I export Claude Code usage separately?


Yes. The CSV spend report lists Claude Code as its own product, and the Claude Enterprise Analytics API returns Claude Code sessions, commits, pull requests and lines of code per user per day. Claude Console organizations can use the Claude Code Analytics API. Claude Code run through Amazon Bedrock does not appear in the Claude Enterprise Analytics API.


## **Measure What the Export Cannot**


Exporting Claude Enterprise data answers who used Claude and how much.
